Q-BLAST-3.purpose: blast radius ranked inside the engine: algo.BFS reach, algo.SSpaths hop distance and bottleneck cap, scored by the faultline.impact UDF (tier weight × 1/(1+hops) × ln(1+traffic+1); $tw = weights.yaml impact.tier_weight)
Q-BLAST-3.cypher:
MATCH (s:Node {id:$id})
CALL {
  WITH s
  CALL algo.SSpaths({sourceNode: s, relTypes: ['PROPAGATES_TO'], weightProp: 'w', relDirection: 'outgoing', maxLen: 8, pathCount: 1000}) YIELD path
  WITH last(nodes(path)) AS n, length(path) AS h, reduce(c = 1.0, r IN relationships(path) | CASE WHEN r.cap < c THEN r.cap ELSE c END) AS bottleneck
  WITH n, min(h) AS hops, max(bottleneck) AS max_cap
  RETURN collect({id: n.id, hops: hops, max_cap: max_cap}) AS reach_hops
}
CALL algo.BFS(s, 8, 'PROPAGATES_TO') YIELD nodes
UNWIND nodes AS n
WITH n, [x IN reach_hops WHERE x.id = n.id][0] AS h
WITH n, h.hops AS hops, h.max_cap AS max_cap
RETURN n.id AS id, [x IN labels(n) WHERE x <> 'Node'][0] AS label, n.tier AS tier, n.revenue_path AS revenue,
       hops, max_cap, faultline.round4(faultline.impact($tw, n.tier, hops, coalesce(max_cap, 0.0) * 100)) AS impact
ORDER BY impact DESC, id
LIMIT 100

Q-CHAIN-MON.purpose: why alerts missed it: for each hop of the proven causal chain, the alerts that fired on it (and when) and whether it has telemetry at all
Q-CHAIN-MON.cypher:
UNWIND range(0, size($chain) - 1) AS i
MATCH (n:Node {id: $chain[i]})
RETURN i AS hop, n.id AS id, [x IN labels(n) WHERE x <> 'Node'][0] AS label,
       [(a:Alert)-[:FIRED_ON]->(n) WHERE a.fired_at >= $since AND a.fired_at <= $until | {id: a.id, at: a.fired_at, metric: a.metric}] AS alerts,
       size([(m:MetricWindow)-[:WINDOW_OF]->(n) | m]) > 0 AS has_telemetry
ORDER BY hop
LIMIT 20

Q-CHANGE-2.purpose: a change's details (kind, time, actor, title, what it touched, the facts it asserts)
Q-CHANGE-2.cypher:
MATCH (d:Deploy {id:$id})
OPTIONAL MATCH (d)-[:CHANGED]->(t:Node)
RETURN d.id AS id, d.kind AS kind, d.at AS at, d.title AS title, d.actor_id AS actor, d.sha AS sha, t.id AS target,
       [(d)-[:ASSERTS]->(f:ChangeFact) | [f.key, f.value]] AS facts
LIMIT 1

Q-CHOKE-1.purpose: chokepoints: betweenness over service calls (seeded sampling → identical every run)
Q-CHOKE-1.cypher:
CALL algo.betweenness({nodeLabels: ['Service', 'Datastore'], relationshipTypes: ['CALLS'], samplingSize: 64, samplingSeed: 42}) YIELD node, score
RETURN node.id AS id, score
ORDER BY score DESC, id
LIMIT 10

Q-CODE-1.purpose: code specialist (diff_summary): what the graph knows about one change's code. The component it CHANGED; the commits it CONTAINS, the files they TOUCH and the component each file is PART_OF; the PRs that contain those commits; the commit authors; the typed facts its diff ASSERTS. code_on_target / facts_on_target say whether that code lands on the CHANGED component. There is no function-level code graph: a file path is the finest grain
Q-CODE-1.cypher:
MATCH (d:Deploy {id:$id})
OPTIONAL MATCH (d)-[:CHANGED]->(t:Node)
RETURN d.id AS id, d.kind AS kind, d.at AS at, d.sha AS sha, t.id AS target,
       [(d)-[:CONTAINS]->(c:Commit) | c.id] AS commits,
       [(d)-[:CONTAINS]->(:Commit)-[:TOUCHES]->(f:File) | f.id] AS files,
       [(d)-[:CONTAINS]->(:Commit)-[:TOUCHES]->(:File)-[:PART_OF]->(x:Node) | x.id] AS file_components,
       [(d)-[:CONTAINS]->(:Commit)<-[:CONTAINS]-(p:PR) | p.id] AS prs,
       [(d)-[:CONTAINS]->(:Commit)<-[:AUTHORED]-(a:Person) | a.id] AS authors,
       [(d)-[:ASSERTS]->(cf:ChangeFact) | [cf.key, cf.file_id]] AS facts,
       size([(d)-[:CONTAINS]->(:Commit)-[:TOUCHES]->(:File)-[:PART_OF]->(t) | 1]) > 0 AS code_on_target,
       size([(d)-[:ASSERTS]->(:ChangeFact)-[:ABOUT]->(t) | 1]) > 0 AS facts_on_target
LIMIT 1

Q-CONN-2.purpose: containment precondition (algo.WCC): is the failing component in the same connected component as anything protected? (no → nothing to cut)
Q-CONN-2.cypher:
CALL algo.WCC({nodeLabels: ['Service', 'Datastore', 'Table', 'KPI', 'Dashboard'], relationshipTypes: ['PROPAGATES_TO']}) YIELD node, componentId
WITH componentId, collect(node.id) AS members
WHERE $target IN members
RETURN componentId, [p IN $protect WHERE p IN members] AS protected_in_component, size(members) AS size
ORDER BY componentId
LIMIT 1

Q-CTX-1.purpose: context of any target: owner team, current on-call, runbooks, active decisions
Q-CTX-1.cypher:
MATCH (s:Node {id:$id})
OPTIONAL MATCH (t:Team)-[:OWNS]->(s)
OPTIONAL MATCH (p:Person)-[oc:ON_CALL]->(t)
WHERE oc.from <= $now AND $now < oc.to AND p.active
OPTIONAL MATCH (r:Runbook)-[:RUNBOOK_FOR]->(s)
WHERE r.valid_to IS NULL
OPTIONAL MATCH (d:Decision {status:'active'})-[:CONSTRAINS]->(s)
RETURN s.id AS id, [x IN labels(s) WHERE x <> 'Node'][0] AS label, t.id AS team,
       collect(DISTINCT p.id) AS oncall, collect(DISTINCT r.id) AS runbooks, collect(DISTINCT d.id) AS decisions
LIMIT 1

Q-CUT-3.purpose: containment in ONE read-only query: algo.maxFlow from $failing to the protected set over cut_cost, then the min-cut inside the engine. Residual reachability from $failing runs over every PROPAGATES_TO edge of the region algo.SSpaths reaches (forward while cut_cost − flow > 1e-9, backward while flow > 1e-9), iterated to a fixpoint as a list reduction; the cut is the edges leaving that source side. A region of $max_edges candidate edges or more skips the fixpoint (the code refuses it). The code only checks that the cut capacity equals maxFlow and that no protected node is on the source side.
Q-CUT-3.cypher:
MATCH (f:Node {id:$failing})
MATCH (p:Node) WHERE p.id IN $protect
WITH f, collect(p.id) AS prot
WHERE size(prot) > 0
CALL {
  WITH f
  CALL algo.SSpaths({sourceNode: f, relTypes: ['PROPAGATES_TO'], weightProp: 'w', relDirection: 'outgoing', maxLen: 8, pathCount: 1000}) YIELD path
  WITH f, collect(DISTINCT last(nodes(path))) + [f] AS region
  UNWIND region AS a
  MATCH (a)-[r:PROPAGATES_TO]->(b)
  WHERE b IN region
  WITH a, r, b ORDER BY a.id, b.id
  RETURN collect({rid: id(r), u: a.id, v: b.id, cost: coalesce(r.cut_cost, 0), domain: r.domain}) AS cand
}
MATCH (t:Node) WHERE t.id IN prot
WITH f, prot, cand, collect(t) AS targets
CALL algo.maxFlow({sourceNodes: [f], targetNodes: targets, relationshipTypes: ['PROPAGATES_TO'], capacityProperty: 'cut_cost'}) YIELD edges, edgeFlows, maxFlow
WITH f, prot, cand, maxFlow,
     [i IN range(0, size(edges) - 1) | {rid: id(edges[i]), u: startNode(edges[i]).id, v: endNode(edges[i]).id, flow: edgeFlows[i]}] AS fe
WITH f, prot, cand, maxFlow, fe,
     [c IN CASE WHEN size(cand) < $max_edges THEN cand ELSE [] END |
      {u: c.u, v: c.v, cost: c.cost, domain: c.domain,
       flow: coalesce(head([x IN fe WHERE x.rid = c.rid | x.flow]), 0)}] AS arcs
WITH f, prot, cand, maxFlow, fe, arcs,
     [a IN arcs WHERE a.cost - a.flow > 1e-9 | [a.u, a.v]] + [a IN arcs WHERE a.flow > 1e-9 | [a.v, a.u]] AS residual
WITH f, prot, cand, maxFlow, fe, arcs,
     reduce(s = [f.id], i IN range(0, size(arcs)) | s + reduce(add = [], x IN residual |
            CASE WHEN x[0] IN s AND NOT x[1] IN s AND NOT x[1] IN add THEN add + [x[1]] ELSE add END)) AS reach
WITH f, prot, cand, maxFlow, fe, arcs, CASE WHEN maxFlow <= 1e-9 THEN [f.id] ELSE reach END AS side
WITH prot, cand, maxFlow, fe, side,
     [a IN arcs WHERE maxFlow > 1e-9 AND a.u IN side AND NOT a.v IN side AND a.cost > 1e-9 |
      {u: a.u, v: a.v, cut_cost: a.cost, domain: a.domain}] AS cut
RETURN cut, reduce(total = 0, c IN cut | total + c.cut_cost) AS cut_total, maxFlow AS max_flow, side AS source_side,
       [x IN prot WHERE x IN side] AS protected_on_source_side, size(cand) AS candidates,
       [e IN fe | [e.u, e.v]] AS flow_edges
LIMIT 1

Q-DEC-1.purpose: gate G8 / preflight: active, non-superseded decisions constraining what a change asserts about; with the reviewer override recorded for THIS change, if any (intentional / accidental / discuss); an override counts only while the change still asserts the value it was given for (a re-push with another value brings the violation back)
Q-DEC-1.cypher:
MATCH (src:Node {id:$change})-[:ASSERTS]->(f:ChangeFact)-[:ABOUT]->(n)<-[:CONSTRAINS]-(d:Decision {status:'active'})
WHERE f.key = d.rule_key AND NOT (d)<-[:SUPERSEDES]-(:Decision {status:'active'})
RETURN d.id AS decision, d.title AS title, d.rule_key AS rule_key, d.rule_op AS op, d.rule_value AS expected,
       f.value AS actual, toString(f.value) AS actual_text, d.url AS url, n.id AS about,
       head([(d)<-[:OVERRIDES]-(o:Override) WHERE o.change_id = $change AND o.actual = toString(f.value) |
             {verdict: o.verdict, by: o.by, why: o.why, at: o.at}]) AS override
ORDER BY decision, about
LIMIT 20

Q-FUTURE-1.purpose: futures (CONTAIN): the predicted residual of the confirmed origin's fault at each target once a containment option is in place, read on that option's own GRAPH.COPY branch (its cut edges already removed; the live run graph for an option that cuts nothing). Model (the gate's and Q-VERIFY-ALLOW's, sim/telemetry.py): a node's excess rises by at most the sum over its in-edges of cap x the source's excess, so the origin's share at t is at most its excess x transfer, the sum over its PROPAGATES_TO paths of 1..8 hops (gate.max_len) of the product of the caps (the origin itself: transfer 1). Excess = the origin's peak since $since minus its mean over the pre-onset baseline, floored at 0, from its MetricWindows: what the graph measured, never the scenario's injected effect. residual = min(1, transfer x excess); 0 when the option removes the origin's fault ($removes_origin: rollback, data repair). Unknown (null) when the excess is unmeasured, an edge has no cap, or more than 1000 paths. Each target also returns its baseline windows (base_vals) and its peak since $since, so the caller applies VERIFY's own band rule
Q-FUTURE-1.cypher:
MATCH (o:Node {id: $origin})
CALL {
  WITH o
  MATCH (w:MetricWindow {target_id: o.id, metric: 'error_rate', kind: 'live'})
  WHERE w.at >= $base_since AND w.at <= $until
  RETURN avg(CASE WHEN w.at <= $base_until THEN w.value END) AS obase, max(CASE WHEN w.at >= $since THEN w.value END) AS opeak
}
WITH o, CASE WHEN opeak IS NULL OR obase IS NULL THEN null WHEN opeak - obase > 0.0 THEN opeak - obase ELSE 0.0 END AS excess
MATCH (t:Node) WHERE t.id IN $targets
CALL {
  WITH o, t
  OPTIONAL MATCH p = (o)-[:PROPAGATES_TO*1..8]->(t)
  WITH p LIMIT 1001
  RETURN count(p) AS paths, min(length(p)) AS hops,
         sum(CASE WHEN p IS NOT NULL AND any(r IN relationships(p) WHERE r.cap IS NULL) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS uncapped,
         sum(CASE WHEN p IS NULL THEN 0.0 ELSE reduce(acc = 1.0, r IN relationships(p) | acc * coalesce(r.cap, 1.0)) END) AS walk
}
CALL {
  WITH t
  MATCH (w:MetricWindow {target_id: t.id, metric: 'error_rate', kind: 'live'})
  WHERE w.at >= $base_since AND w.at <= $until
  RETURN collect(CASE WHEN w.at <= $base_until THEN w.value END) AS base_vals,
         max(CASE WHEN w.at >= $since THEN w.value END) AS peak
}
WITH o, t, excess, paths, hops, base_vals, peak,
     CASE WHEN t.id = o.id THEN 1.0 WHEN paths > 1000 OR uncapped > 0 THEN null ELSE walk END AS transfer
RETURN t.id AS target, o.id AS origin, t.id = o.id AS is_origin, CASE WHEN t.id = o.id THEN 0 ELSE hops END AS hops,
       paths, transfer, excess, base_vals, peak,
       CASE WHEN $removes_origin THEN 0.0
            WHEN excess IS NULL OR transfer IS NULL THEN null
            WHEN transfer * excess > 1.0 THEN 1.0 ELSE transfer * excess END AS residual
ORDER BY target
LIMIT 50

Q-GATE-1.purpose: THE load-bearing query (gate G2): shortest causal paths cause → symptom. Empty = no path, no claim. learned_from names, per hop, the incident whose verified fix taught a learned link ('' for an ordinary edge), so a proof that relies on one says so
Q-GATE-1.cypher:
MATCH (c:Node {id:$cause}), (s:Node {id:$symptom})
CALL algo.SPpaths({sourceNode: c, targetNode: s, relTypes: ['CHANGED', 'GATES', 'PROPAGATES_TO'], weightProp: 'w', relDirection: 'outgoing', maxLen: 8, pathCount: 3}) YIELD path, pathWeight
RETURN [n IN nodes(path) | n.id] AS chain, [r IN relationships(path) | type(r)] AS rels, pathWeight AS weight, length(path) AS hops,
       [r IN relationships(path) | coalesce(r.from_incident, '')] AS learned_from
ORDER BY weight, hops
LIMIT 3

Q-GATE-2.purpose: gate G3 time order: is the cause inside the window, and is there an earlier upstream change on its path?
Q-GATE-2.cypher:
MATCH (c:Deploy {id:$cause})-[:CHANGED]->(cs)
OPTIONAL MATCH (cs)-[:DEPENDS_ON*1..8]->(up)<-[:CHANGED]-(earlier:Deploy)
WHERE earlier.at < c.at AND earlier.at >= $onset - $window_ms
RETURN c.at <= $onset AND $onset <= c.at + $window_ms AS in_window, c.at AS cause_at, $onset AS onset_at,
       collect(DISTINCT earlier.id) AS earlier_upstream_changes
LIMIT 1

Q-GATE-3.purpose: gate G5 sufficiency bound: max share of the symptom that the source set can explain (single or joint)
Q-GATE-3.cypher:
MATCH (s:Node) WHERE s.id IN $sources
WITH collect(s) AS srcs
WHERE size(srcs) > 0
MATCH (t:Node {id:$symptom})
CALL algo.maxFlow({sourceNodes: srcs, targetNodes: [t], relationshipTypes: ['PROPAGATES_TO'], capacityProperty: 'cap'}) YIELD maxFlow
RETURN maxFlow AS max_flow, size(srcs) AS sources
LIMIT 1

Q-GATE-4.purpose: gate G4: cited quantitative evidence produced by this run that is ABOUT a node on the causal chain
Q-GATE-4.cypher:
MATCH (run:Run {id:$run})-[:HAS_TOOL_CALL]->(:ToolCall)-[:PRODUCED_EVIDENCE]->(e:Evidence)-[:ABOUT]->(n:Node)
WHERE e.id IN $evidence AND n.id IN $chain AND e.kind IN ['metric', 'profile', 'baseline_comparison', 'row_share', 'error_rate']
RETURN e.id AS evidence, n.id AS about, e.kind AS kind, e.ratio AS ratio, e.band AS band, e.value AS value,
       e.baseline AS baseline, e.anomalous AS anomalous, e.summary AS summary
ORDER BY evidence, about
LIMIT 50

Q-GATE-7.purpose: gate G7 agreement: independent channels (sources) whose cited evidence is ABOUT nodes of the causal chain
Q-GATE-7.cypher:
MATCH (run:Run {id:$run})-[:HAS_TOOL_CALL]->(:ToolCall)-[:PRODUCED_EVIDENCE]->(e:Evidence)-[:ABOUT]->(n:Node)
WHERE e.id IN $evidence AND n.id IN $chain
RETURN e.source AS source, collect(DISTINCT e.id) AS evidence, collect(DISTINCT n.id) AS about
ORDER BY source
LIMIT 20

Q-GATE-CORR.purpose: gate G7 structural correlation: for every specialist report of this run (a done specialist Task; crew step records are never votes), the deploys it NAMES, and the chain nodes it reaches by naming the cause Deploy through its CHANGED edge (non-empty `via` = this report names the cause, and the cause CHANGED a node of the G2 chain)
Q-GATE-CORR.cypher:
MATCH (run:Run {id:$run})-[:HAS_TASK]->(t:Task)
WHERE t.state = 'done' AND t.kind = 'specialist' AND t.role IN $roles
RETURN t.role AS role, t.status AS status, t.id AS task,
       [(t)-[:NAMES]->(d:Deploy) | d.id] AS named,
       [(t)-[:NAMES]->(d:Deploy)-[:CHANGED]->(x:Node) WHERE d.id = $cause AND x.id IN $chain | x.id] AS via
ORDER BY role, task
LIMIT 20

Q-GATE-G1.purpose: gate G1 grounding: which of $ids this run SAW in graph results, and which cited evidence ids it produced
Q-GATE-G1.cypher:
MATCH (run:Run {id:$run})
RETURN [(run)-[:HAS_TOOL_CALL]->(:ToolCall)-[:SAW]->(n:Node) WHERE n.id IN $ids | n.id] AS seen,
       [(run)-[:HAS_TOOL_CALL]->(:ToolCall)-[:PRODUCED_EVIDENCE]->(e:Evidence) WHERE e.id IN $evidence | e.id] AS evidence
LIMIT 1

Q-GATE-MULT.purpose: G5 multiplicity per suspect: how many distinct failure paths (up to 100, algo.SPpaths) lead from each source to the symptom. A request can meet the same fault once per path, so a source's sound G5 bound is min(1, k × maxFlow); k = 1 leaves it unchanged (gate bench / G5 property finding)
Q-GATE-MULT.cypher:
MATCH (t:Node {id: $symptom})
UNWIND $sources AS sid
MATCH (s:Node {id: sid})
CALL algo.SPpaths({sourceNode: s, targetNode: t, relTypes: ['PROPAGATES_TO'], weightProp: 'w', relDirection: 'outgoing', maxLen: 8, pathCount: 100}) YIELD path
RETURN s.id AS source, count(path) AS paths
ORDER BY source
LIMIT 100

Q-GATE-UPSTREAM.purpose: sweep, G4 upstream ELIMINATION under a strict lower bound (deep bench + adversarial review): for each suspect's changed component s, a component u upstream whose own measured fault fully accounts for s's anomaly: u's excess >= $min_excess, u's anomaly started no later than s's, no failure path leads back from s to u, and s's excess <= u's excess x the BEST SINGLE path's product of cap x share (share = the call share recorded on each PROPAGATES_TO edge at ingest, the propagation the services actually see; a hop without a share, e.g. data plane or a learned link, makes the path unusable). No slack: any surplus at s may be its own fault, so s stays a candidate. Excess = peak since $since minus the pre-onset baseline mean; onset = the first window after the baseline whose rise is >= $min_excess
Q-GATE-UPSTREAM.cypher:
MATCH (s:Node) WHERE s.id IN $ids
MATCH (u:Node)-[:PROPAGATES_TO*1..8]->(s)
WITH DISTINCT u, s
CALL {
  WITH u, s
  OPTIONAL MATCH back = (s)-[:PROPAGATES_TO*1..8]->(u)
  WITH back LIMIT 1
  RETURN count(back) AS backpaths
}
CALL {
  WITH s
  MATCH (w:MetricWindow {target_id: s.id, metric: 'error_rate', kind: 'live'})
  WHERE w.at >= $base_since AND w.at <= $until
  WITH collect(w) AS ws
  WITH ws, [x IN ws WHERE x.at <= $base_until | x.value] AS bv
  WITH ws, CASE WHEN size(bv) = 0 THEN null ELSE reduce(a = 0.0, v IN bv | a + v) / size(bv) END AS base
  RETURN base AS sbase,
         reduce(m = null, x IN ws | CASE WHEN x.at >= $since AND (m IS NULL OR x.value > m) THEN x.value ELSE m END) AS speak,
         reduce(o = null, x IN ws | CASE WHEN base IS NOT NULL AND x.at > $base_until AND x.value - base >= $min_excess
                                          AND (o IS NULL OR x.at < o) THEN x.at ELSE o END) AS sonset
}
CALL {
  WITH u
  MATCH (w:MetricWindow {target_id: u.id, metric: 'error_rate', kind: 'live'})
  WHERE w.at >= $base_since AND w.at <= $until
  WITH collect(w) AS ws
  WITH ws, [x IN ws WHERE x.at <= $base_until | x.value] AS bv
  WITH ws, CASE WHEN size(bv) = 0 THEN null ELSE reduce(a = 0.0, v IN bv | a + v) / size(bv) END AS base
  RETURN base AS ubase,
         reduce(m = null, x IN ws | CASE WHEN x.at >= $since AND (m IS NULL OR x.value > m) THEN x.value ELSE m END) AS upeak,
         reduce(o = null, x IN ws | CASE WHEN base IS NOT NULL AND x.at > $base_until AND x.value - base >= $min_excess
                                          AND (o IS NULL OR x.at < o) THEN x.at ELSE o END) AS uonset
}
CALL {
  WITH u, s
  MATCH p = (u)-[:PROPAGATES_TO*1..8]->(s)
  WITH p LIMIT 1001
  WITH p, all(r IN relationships(p) WHERE r.cap IS NOT NULL AND r.share IS NOT NULL) AS usable
  RETURN count(p) AS paths, min(length(p)) AS hops,
         max(CASE WHEN usable THEN reduce(acc = 1.0, r IN relationships(p) | acc * r.cap * r.share) END) AS best
}
WITH u, s, hops, backpaths, sonset, uonset,
     CASE WHEN speak IS NULL OR sbase IS NULL THEN null WHEN speak - sbase > 0.0 THEN speak - sbase ELSE 0.0 END AS sex,
     CASE WHEN upeak IS NULL OR ubase IS NULL THEN null WHEN upeak - ubase > 0.0 THEN upeak - ubase ELSE 0.0 END AS uex,
     CASE WHEN paths > 1000 THEN null ELSE best END AS transfer
WITH u, s, hops, backpaths, sonset, uonset, sex, uex, transfer,
     CASE WHEN transfer IS NULL OR uex IS NULL THEN null WHEN transfer * uex > 1.0 THEN 1.0 ELSE transfer * uex END AS carried
WHERE sex IS NOT NULL AND sex > 0.0 AND uex IS NOT NULL AND uex >= $min_excess AND backpaths = 0
  AND carried IS NOT NULL AND sex <= carried
  AND uonset IS NOT NULL AND sonset IS NOT NULL AND uonset <= sonset
RETURN s.id AS s, u.id AS u, hops, transfer, uex AS u_excess, sex AS s_excess, carried, uonset AS u_onset, sonset AS s_onset
ORDER BY s, hops, u
LIMIT 100

Q-GATE-UPSTREAM-UB.purpose: confirm phase, G4 upstream DOWNGRADE-ONLY check (deep bench + adversarial review): for the confirmed change's components s, any component u upstream (a failure path of 1..8 hops, no path back) whose measured excess could carry s's under the GENEROUS upper bound: s's excess <= min(1, u's excess x transfer) x $slack, transfer = Q-FUTURE-1's model (sum over the PROPAGATES_TO paths of the product of the caps), u's excess >= $min_excess. A row means the change may not be the origin, so the claim is downgraded to not confident; it never eliminates anything (an upper bound may only make the gate more careful). Excess = peak since $since minus the pre-onset baseline mean, from MetricWindows
Q-GATE-UPSTREAM-UB.cypher:
MATCH (s:Node) WHERE s.id IN $ids
MATCH (u:Node)-[:PROPAGATES_TO*1..8]->(s)
WITH DISTINCT u, s
CALL {
  WITH s
  MATCH (w:MetricWindow {target_id: s.id, metric: 'error_rate', kind: 'live'})
  WHERE w.at >= $base_since AND w.at <= $until
  RETURN avg(CASE WHEN w.at <= $base_until THEN w.value END) AS sbase, max(CASE WHEN w.at >= $since THEN w.value END) AS speak
}
CALL {
  WITH u
  MATCH (w:MetricWindow {target_id: u.id, metric: 'error_rate', kind: 'live'})
  WHERE w.at >= $base_since AND w.at <= $until
  RETURN avg(CASE WHEN w.at <= $base_until THEN w.value END) AS ubase, max(CASE WHEN w.at >= $since THEN w.value END) AS upeak
}
CALL {
  WITH u, s
  MATCH p = (u)-[:PROPAGATES_TO*1..8]->(s)
  WITH p LIMIT 1001
  RETURN count(p) AS paths, min(length(p)) AS hops,
         sum(CASE WHEN any(r IN relationships(p) WHERE r.cap IS NULL) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS uncapped,
         sum(reduce(acc = 1.0, r IN relationships(p) | acc * coalesce(r.cap, 1.0))) AS walk
}
CALL {
  WITH u, s
  OPTIONAL MATCH back = (s)-[:PROPAGATES_TO*1..8]->(u)
  WITH back LIMIT 1
  RETURN count(back) AS backpaths
}
WITH u, s, hops, backpaths,
     CASE WHEN speak IS NULL OR sbase IS NULL THEN null WHEN speak - sbase > 0.0 THEN speak - sbase ELSE 0.0 END AS sex,
     CASE WHEN upeak IS NULL OR ubase IS NULL THEN null WHEN upeak - ubase > 0.0 THEN upeak - ubase ELSE 0.0 END AS uex,
     CASE WHEN paths > 1000 OR uncapped > 0 THEN null ELSE walk END AS transfer
WITH u, s, hops, backpaths, sex, uex, transfer,
     CASE WHEN transfer IS NULL OR uex IS NULL THEN null WHEN transfer * uex > 1.0 THEN 1.0 ELSE transfer * uex END AS carried
WHERE sex IS NOT NULL AND sex > 0.0 AND uex IS NOT NULL AND uex >= $min_excess AND backpaths = 0
  AND carried IS NOT NULL AND sex <= carried * $slack
RETURN s.id AS s, u.id AS u, hops, transfer, uex AS u_excess, sex AS s_excess, carried
ORDER BY s, hops, u
LIMIT 100

Q-HYP-1.purpose: hypotheses of an incident with the evidence that supports/refutes them (gate G6, UI)
Q-HYP-1.cypher:
MATCH (i:Incident {id:$inc})-[:HYPOTHESIZES]->(h:Hypothesis)-[:BLAMES]->(c:Node)
OPTIONAL MATCH (e:Evidence)-[:SUPPORTS]->(h)
OPTIONAL MATCH (e2:Evidence)-[:REFUTES]->(h)
RETURN h.id AS id, c.id AS cause, h.status AS status, h.score AS score, h.reason AS reason, h.origin AS origin,
       coalesce(h.status_by, h.origin) AS status_by,
       collect(DISTINCT e.id) AS supports, collect(DISTINCT e2.id) AS refutes
ORDER BY id
LIMIT 50

Q-LIN-1.cypher:
MATCH (sym:Node {id:$symptom})
CALL algo.SSpaths({sourceNode: sym, relTypes: ['DEPENDS_ON'], weightProp: 'w', relDirection: 'outgoing', maxLen: 8, pathCount: 1000}) YIELD path
WITH last(nodes(path)) AS n, min(length(path)) AS hops
RETURN n.id AS id, [x IN labels(n) WHERE x <> 'Node'][0] AS label, hops
ORDER BY hops, id
LIMIT 100

Q-MEM-1.purpose: recall (recency = 0.5^(age/half-life), scenario clock via onset_at): vector seed (the incident's own embedding in the FalkorDB vector index) → structural confirmation (a shared Symptom node) → ranked by (1 - $w_recency) × similarity + $w_recency × recency (among look-alikes the recent one first; $w_recency 0 is similarity only); returns what fixed it before and how long ago it was last seen
Q-MEM-1.cypher:
MATCH (cur:Incident {id:$current})
CALL db.idx.vector.queryNodes('Incident', 'embedding', 10, cur.embedding) YIELD node, score
WITH cur, node, score
WHERE node.id <> cur.id AND (node)-[:HAS_SYMPTOM]->(:Symptom)<-[:HAS_SYMPTOM]-(cur)
WITH cur, node, score, toFloat($now - coalesce(node.onset_at, node.opened_at)) AS age_ms
WITH cur, node, score, age_ms,
     CASE WHEN age_ms <= 0 THEN 1.0 ELSE exp(-0.6931471805599453 * age_ms / $half_life_ms) END AS recency
RETURN node.id AS id, node.title AS title, score AS distance, 1.0 - score AS similarity, node.salience AS salience,
       node.opened_at AS opened_at, recency, age_ms,
       (1.0 - $w_recency) * (1.0 - score) + $w_recency * recency AS rank_score,
       [(node)-[:HAS_SYMPTOM]->(sy:Symptom)<-[:HAS_SYMPTOM]-(cur) | sy.id] AS shared,
       [(node)-[:RESOLVED_BY]->(a:Action) WHERE a.verdict = 'APPLIED' | a.kind] AS fixes,
       [(t:Node)<-[:CHANGED]-(:Deploy)-[:CAUSED]->(node) | t.id] AS cause_targets,
       [(pm:Postmortem)-[:DOCUMENTS]->(node) | pm.summary] AS postmortem
ORDER BY rank_score DESC, distance, id
LIMIT 5

Q-MEM-3.purpose: procedural memory first: current runbooks for the given components/symptoms (derived ones before human ones, then by support)
Q-MEM-3.cypher:
MATCH (r:Runbook)-[:RUNBOOK_FOR]->(x:Node)
WHERE x.id IN $ids AND r.valid_to IS NULL
WITH r, collect(DISTINCT x.id) AS for_ids
RETURN r.id AS id, r.title AS title, r.source AS source, coalesce(r.salience, 1.0) AS salience,
       coalesce(r.support_count, 0) AS support, r.steps AS steps, for_ids,
       [(r)-[:DERIVED_FROM]->(pm:Postmortem) | pm.id] AS derived_from
ORDER BY CASE r.source WHEN 'derived' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, support DESC, salience DESC, id
LIMIT 10

Q-MEM-4.purpose: what an incident recalled at RECALL (the RECALLED edges written then): similarity, recency, salience and the fixes that worked
Q-MEM-4.cypher:
MATCH (cur:Incident {id:$inc})-[r:RECALLED]->(p:Incident)
RETURN p.id AS id, p.title AS title, r.similarity AS similarity, r.recency AS recency, r.salience AS salience,
       r.shared AS shared,
       [(p)-[:RESOLVED_BY|ATTEMPTED]->(a:Action) | {kind: a.kind, verdict: a.verdict, target: a.target_id}] AS actions,
       [(t:Node)<-[:CHANGED]-(:Deploy)-[:CAUSED]->(p) | t.id] AS cause_targets
ORDER BY similarity DESC, id
LIMIT 10

Q-MEM-5.purpose: what the recalled precedents teach about each fix kind: how often it was APPLIED vs NOT_APPLIED (procedural memory for the plan)
Q-MEM-5.cypher:
MATCH (cur:Incident {id:$inc})-[:RECALLED]->(p:Incident)-[:RESOLVED_BY|ATTEMPTED]->(a:Action)
RETURN a.kind AS kind, a.verdict AS verdict, count(DISTINCT p) AS n, collect(DISTINCT p.id) AS incidents
ORDER BY kind, verdict
LIMIT 20

Q-MEM-6.purpose: incident families: algo.labelPropagation over incidents, their symptoms and the components their causes changed (read-only, on the tenant graph); the family holding $inc first
Q-MEM-6.cypher:
CALL algo.labelPropagation({nodeLabels: ['Incident', 'Symptom', 'Deploy', 'Service', 'Datastore', 'Transform', 'Table'], relationshipTypes: ['HAS_SYMPTOM', 'CAUSED', 'CHANGED'], maxIterations: 20}) YIELD node, communityId
WITH communityId, collect(CASE WHEN 'Incident' IN labels(node) THEN node.id END) AS incidents
WHERE size(incidents) >= 2
RETURN communityId, incidents, size(incidents) AS size, $inc IN incidents AS mine
ORDER BY mine DESC, size DESC, communityId
LIMIT 50

Q-NOTE-RECALL.purpose: shared agent notes (T2), recalled in ONE query on agentmem_<tenant> by meaning (vecf32 index over the note text, cosine ≥ $floor) and by graph distance (notes about $focus or a component within $hops PROPAGATES_TO hops either way), unexpired on the engine clock, shared or the $viewer's own private notes, ranked inside the engine by faultline.noteScore ($w = weights.yaml notes), with each note's components and its replies; no `seen` column: a note is a lead, never evidence for the gate (G1)
Q-NOTE-RECALL.cypher:
CALL {
  UNWIND CASE WHEN $focus = '' THEN [] ELSE [1] END AS one
  MATCH p = (f:Node {id: $focus})-[:PROPAGATES_TO*0..3]-(x:Node)
  WHERE length(p) <= $hops
  WITH x, min(length(p)) AS h
  MATCH (n:Note)-[:ABOUT]->(x)
  RETURN n, h AS hops, null AS sim
  UNION ALL
  UNWIND CASE WHEN $q IS NULL THEN [] ELSE [1] END AS one
  CALL db.idx.vector.queryNodes('Note', 'embedding', 20, vecf32($q)) YIELD node, score
  WITH node, 1.0 - score AS sim WHERE sim >= $floor
  RETURN node AS n, null AS hops, sim
}
WITH n, min(hops) AS hops, max(sim) AS sim
WHERE n.expires_at > timestamp() AND (coalesce(n.visibility, 'shared') = 'shared' OR n.agent = $viewer)
WITH n, hops, sim, faultline.noteScore($w, sim, hops, (timestamp() - n.created_at) / 60000.0) AS score
RETURN n.id AS id, n.agent AS agent, n.name AS name, n.kind AS kind, n.text AS text, n.created_at AS created_at,
       n.expires_at AS expires_at, [(n)-[:ABOUT]->(c) | c.id] AS about, hops, faultline.round4(sim) AS similarity,
       [x IN [(r:Note)-[rt:REPLY_TO]->(n) | {id: r.id, agent: r.agent, stance: rt.stance, text: r.text,
                                              shared: coalesce(r.visibility, 'shared') = 'shared'}]
        WHERE x.shared OR x.agent = $viewer | {id: x.id, agent: x.agent, stance: x.stance, text: x.text}] AS replies,
       coalesce(n.visibility, 'shared') AS visibility,
       faultline.round4(score) AS score
ORDER BY score DESC, id
LIMIT 20

Q-NOTIFY-2.purpose: who to NOTIFY (not who fixes), ranked inside the engine: algo.SSpaths blast radius of $id (hops, bottleneck cap), the teams owning each impacted node, their summed faultline.capImpact (tier weight × cap / (1+hops); $tw = weights.yaml impact.tier_weight), the nearest hop, the $priority nodes they own and who is on call for them at $now
Q-NOTIFY-2.cypher:
MATCH (s:Node {id:$id})
CALL algo.SSpaths({sourceNode: s, relTypes: ['PROPAGATES_TO'], weightProp: 'w', relDirection: 'outgoing', maxLen: 8, pathCount: 1000}) YIELD path
WITH last(nodes(path)) AS n, length(path) AS h, reduce(c = 1.0, r IN relationships(path) | CASE WHEN r.cap < c THEN r.cap ELSE c END) AS bottleneck
WITH n, min(h) AS hops, max(bottleneck) AS max_cap
WHERE n.id <> $id
MATCH (t:Team)-[:OWNS]->(n)
WITH DISTINCT t, n, hops, max_cap
WITH t, collect(n.id) AS owns_impacted, sum(faultline.capImpact($tw, n.tier, max_cap, hops)) AS impact, min(hops) AS nearest_hops
WITH t, owns_impacted, faultline.round4(impact) AS impact, nearest_hops, [x IN owns_impacted WHERE x IN $priority] AS priority
RETURN t.id AS team, t.name AS name, owns_impacted,
       [x IN [(p:Person)-[oc:ON_CALL]->(t) WHERE oc.from <= $now AND $now < oc.to | p] WHERE x.active | x.id] AS oncall,
       impact, nearest_hops, priority
ORDER BY CASE WHEN size(priority) > 0 THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, impact DESC, team
LIMIT 20

Q-OBL-CUST.purpose: obligation clock: customers reached through the failure. (:Customer)-[:CONSUMES]->(the failing component or anything in its blast radius, algo.BFS over PROPAGATES_TO, 8 hops), ONE row per distinct customer (a customer reached by several paths counts once) with every node that reached them, the nearest failure path (shortestPath) and, on every row, the revenue at risk = sum of mrr over the distinct customers
Q-OBL-CUST.cypher:
MATCH (s:Node {id:$id})
CALL { WITH s CALL algo.BFS(s, 8, 'PROPAGATES_TO') YIELD nodes UNWIND nodes AS x RETURN collect(x) AS reached }
WITH s, reached + [s] AS reach
UNWIND reach AS n
MATCH (c:Customer)-[v:CONSUMES]->(n)
WITH c, n, v.via AS via, shortestPath((s)-[:PROPAGATES_TO*0..8]->(n)) AS p
WITH c, n, via, [x IN nodes(p) | x.id] AS path
ORDER BY size(path), n.id
WITH c, collect(n.id) AS through, collect(via) AS vias, collect(path) AS paths
WITH collect({c: c, through: through, vias: vias, path: paths[0]}) AS reached, sum(c.mrr) AS revenue_at_risk, count(c) AS customers_reached
UNWIND reached AS r
RETURN r.c.id AS customer, r.c.name AS name, r.c.tier AS tier, r.c.mrr AS mrr, r.through AS through, r.vias AS via,
       size(r.through) AS paths, r.path AS path, size(r.path) - 1 AS hops, revenue_at_risk, customers_reached
ORDER BY mrr DESC, customer
LIMIT 100

Q-OBL-SLO.purpose: obligation clock: error-budget burn of every SLO on the failing component and its blast radius (algo.BFS over PROPAGATES_TO, 8 hops). From the (:MetricWindow)-[:WINDOW_OF]-> telemetry: the current error rate (mean over [$current_since, $now]), burn = current rate / budget, and the budget remaining = 1 - spent before the telemetry horizon - error-minutes in the SLO window / budget-minutes
Q-OBL-SLO.cypher:
MATCH (s:Node {id:$id})
CALL { WITH s CALL algo.BFS(s, 8, 'PROPAGATES_TO') YIELD nodes UNWIND nodes AS x RETURN collect(x) AS reached }
UNWIND reached + [s] AS n
MATCH (o:SLO)-[:FOR]->(n)
WITH o, n, [(w:MetricWindow)-[:WINDOW_OF]->(n) WHERE w.kind = 'live' AND w.metric = o.metric AND w.at <= $now AND w.at > $now - o.window_days * 86400000 | w] AS ws
WITH o, n, ws, [w IN ws WHERE w.at >= $current_since | w.value] AS cur
WITH o, n, size(ws) AS windows, size(cur) AS current_windows, reduce(t = 0.0, w IN ws | t + w.value) AS error_minutes,
     CASE WHEN size(cur) = 0 THEN null ELSE reduce(t = 0.0, v IN cur | t + v) / size(cur) END AS error_rate
RETURN o.id AS slo, n.id AS service, [x IN labels(n) WHERE x <> 'Node'][0] AS label, n.tier AS tier,
       o.objective AS objective, o.budget AS budget, o.window_days AS window_days, o.spent_prior AS spent_prior,
       windows, current_windows, error_rate,
       CASE WHEN error_rate IS NULL THEN null ELSE error_rate / o.budget END AS burn,
       1.0 - o.spent_prior - error_minutes / (o.budget * o.window_days * 1440.0) AS budget_remaining
ORDER BY coalesce(burn, -1.0) DESC, slo
LIMIT 100

Q-ORG-BUS.purpose: bus factor in the graph: the fewest ACTIVE people (most commits first) whose commits cover > 50% of the component's commits (0 = nobody active does), plus whether the top contributor has left
Q-ORG-BUS.cypher:
MATCH (s:Node {id:$target})<-[c:COMMITTED]-(p:Person)
WITH p, c ORDER BY c.n DESC, p.id
WITH collect({id: p.id, n: c.n, active: p.active}) AS rows, sum(c.n) AS total
WITH rows, total WHERE size(rows) > 0
WITH rows, total, [x IN rows WHERE x.active] AS act
WITH rows, total, act, [i IN range(0, size(act) - 1) WHERE reduce(acc = 0, x IN act[0..i + 1] | acc + x.n) * 2 > total] AS covering
RETURN total, CASE WHEN size(covering) = 0 THEN 0 ELSE covering[0] + 1 END AS bus_factor,
       rows[0].id AS top_person, NOT coalesce(rows[0].active, true) AS top_contributor_inactive, size(rows) AS committers
LIMIT 1

Q-ORG-COLLAB-W.purpose: escalation weights, computed in Cypher: one row per pair of the given people with any COLLABORATES or REPORTS_TO edge between them (either direction), weight = the strongest tie (a COLLABORATES edge's w, default 1.0; a reporting line 0.5), for algo.MSF (maximize) on a scratch graph
Q-ORG-COLLAB-W.cypher:
MATCH (a:Person)-[r:COLLABORATES|REPORTS_TO]-(b:Person)
WHERE a.id IN $ids AND b.id IN $ids AND a.id < b.id
RETURN a.id AS a, b.id AS b, max(CASE WHEN type(r) = 'COLLABORATES' THEN coalesce(r.w, 1.0) ELSE 0.5 END) AS w
ORDER BY a, b
LIMIT 100

Q-ORG-HARM.purpose: who fixes it: algo.HarmonicCentrality over the symmetric KNOWS_ABOUT scratch projection (people close to the cause's code, incidents and on-call); people only, ranked before the LIMIT, so files and incidents in the projection never push a person out of the top 50 (a top-k read: who_fixes shows 10)
Q-ORG-HARM.cypher:
CALL algo.HarmonicCentrality({nodeLabels: ['Node'], relationshipTypes: ['KNOWS_ABOUT']}) YIELD node, score, reachable
WITH node, score, reachable
WHERE node.kind = 'person'
RETURN node.id AS id, node.kind AS kind, score, reachable
ORDER BY score DESC, id
LIMIT 50

Q-ORG-KNOWS.purpose: who_fixes projection, built in Cypher: the KNOWS_ABOUT pairs around a component, one row per undirected pair, keyset-paged on the (a, b) tuple after ($after_a, $after_b). Pairs: person-file (an active person's commits on the component's files since $since), file-component (every file of the component), person-incident and incident-component (active people who resolved an incident that affected it), person-component (active on-call for the owner team at $now), person-person (COLLABORATES with w >= $min_collab between any two of those people or the owner team's active members). The caller writes each pair both ways into a scratch graph for algo.HarmonicCentrality (Q-ORG-HARM)
Q-ORG-KNOWS.cypher:
MATCH (c:Node {id: $target})
CALL {
  WITH c
  MATCH (t:Team)-[:OWNS]->(c)
  RETURN collect(t.id) AS owner_teams
}
CALL {
  WITH c
  MATCH (c)<-[:PART_OF]-(f:File)<-[:TOUCHES]-(cm:Commit)<-[:AUTHORED]-(p:Person)
  WHERE cm.at >= $since AND p.active
  RETURN collect(DISTINCT [p.id, 'person', f.id, 'file']) AS authored, collect(DISTINCT p.id) AS authors
}
CALL {
  WITH c
  MATCH (f:File)-[:PART_OF]->(c)
  RETURN collect(DISTINCT [f.id, 'file', c.id, 'component']) AS files
}
CALL {
  WITH c
  MATCH (r:Person)-[:RESOLVED]->(i:Incident)-[:AFFECTED]->(c)
  WHERE r.active
  RETURN collect(DISTINCT [r.id, 'person', i.id, 'incident']) + collect(DISTINCT [i.id, 'incident', c.id, 'component']) AS resolved,
         collect(DISTINCT r.id) AS resolvers
}
CALL {
  WITH c, owner_teams
  MATCH (o:Person)-[oc:ON_CALL]->(t:Team)
  WHERE t.id IN owner_teams AND oc.from <= $now AND $now < oc.to AND o.active
  RETURN collect(DISTINCT [o.id, 'person', c.id, 'component']) AS oncall, collect(DISTINCT o.id) AS oncallers
}
CALL {
  WITH owner_teams
  MATCH (m:Person)-[:MEMBER_OF]->(t:Team)
  WHERE t.id IN owner_teams AND m.active
  RETURN collect(DISTINCT m.id) AS members
}
WITH authored + files + resolved + oncall AS pairs, authors + resolvers + oncallers + members AS people
CALL {
  WITH people
  MATCH (a:Person)-[k:COLLABORATES]->(b:Person)
  WHERE a.id IN people AND b.id IN people AND coalesce(k.w, 1.0) >= $min_collab
  RETURN collect(DISTINCT [a.id, 'person', b.id, 'person']) AS collab
}
UNWIND pairs + collab AS e
WITH DISTINCT e[0] AS a, e[1] AS a_kind, e[2] AS b, e[3] AS b_kind
WITH a, a_kind, b, b_kind
WHERE a > $after_a OR (a = $after_a AND b > $after_b)
RETURN a, a_kind, b, b_kind
ORDER BY a, b
LIMIT 100

Q-ORG-MGR.purpose: the reporting chain (managers, ≤3 levels) of a set of people, for escalation
Q-ORG-MGR.cypher:
MATCH (p:Person)-[:REPORTS_TO*1..3]->(m:Person)
WHERE p.id IN $ids AND m.active
RETURN p.id AS person, m.id AS manager
ORDER BY person, manager
LIMIT 100

Q-ORG-MSF.purpose: escalation tree: algo.MSF (maximize w) over the responders and their managers, on a scratch projection; one row per tree edge, strongest tie first (the order is the escalation order, computed here)
Q-ORG-MSF.cypher:
CALL algo.MSF({nodeLabels: ['Node'], relationshipTypes: ['COLLABORATES'], objective: 'maximize', weightAttribute: 'w'}) YIELD edges
UNWIND edges AS e
RETURN startNode(e).id AS from, endNode(e).id AS to, e.w AS w
ORDER BY w DESC, from, to
LIMIT 100

Q-ORG-WHO.purpose: who_fixes people and the reasons for each, computed in Cypher: every active recent author (commits on the component's files since $since), past resolver (an incident that affected it), on-call person of the owner team at $now and active owner-team member, with how many recent commits they made on it, which of its incidents they resolved (sorted), whether they are on call and whether they are an owner-team member; name, teams and the owner team for display. The caller only formats the reasons
Q-ORG-WHO.cypher:
MATCH (c:Node {id: $target})
CALL {
  WITH c
  MATCH (t:Team)-[:OWNS]->(c)
  RETURN collect(t.id) AS owner_teams
}
CALL {
  WITH c
  MATCH (c)<-[:PART_OF]-(:File)<-[:TOUCHES]-(cm:Commit)<-[:AUTHORED]-(p:Person)
  WHERE cm.at >= $since AND p.active
  WITH p.id AS pid, count(DISTINCT cm) AS n
  RETURN collect(pid) AS authors, collect([pid, n]) AS author_commits
}
CALL {
  WITH c
  MATCH (r:Person)-[:RESOLVED]->(i:Incident)-[:AFFECTED]->(c)
  WHERE r.active
  WITH r.id AS pid, i.id AS iid
  ORDER BY pid, iid
  WITH pid, collect(DISTINCT iid) AS iids
  RETURN collect(pid) AS resolvers, collect([pid, iids]) AS resolver_incidents
}
CALL {
  WITH owner_teams
  MATCH (o:Person)-[oc:ON_CALL]->(t:Team)
  WHERE t.id IN owner_teams AND oc.from <= $now AND $now < oc.to AND o.active
  RETURN collect(DISTINCT o.id) AS oncall
}
CALL {
  WITH owner_teams
  MATCH (m:Person)-[:MEMBER_OF]->(t:Team)
  WHERE t.id IN owner_teams AND m.active
  RETURN collect(DISTINCT m.id) AS members
}


UNWIND authors + resolvers + oncall + members AS pid
WITH DISTINCT owner_teams, pid, oncall, members, author_commits, resolver_incidents
MATCH (p:Person {id: pid})
RETURN p.id AS person, p.name AS name, [(p)-[:MEMBER_OF]->(tm:Team) | tm.id] AS teams, owner_teams[0] AS team,
       coalesce(head([x IN author_commits WHERE x[0] = pid | x[1]]), 0) AS commits,
       coalesce(head([x IN resolver_incidents WHERE x[0] = pid | x[1]]), []) AS resolved,
       pid IN oncall AS oncall, pid IN members AS member
ORDER BY person
LIMIT 100

Q-OWN-AT.purpose: ownership over time: every OWNED_AT period of a component, which one covered time $at, and which is current
Q-OWN-AT.cypher:
MATCH (t:Team)-[o:OWNED_AT]->(n:Node {id: $id})
RETURN t.id AS team, t.name AS name, o.from AS since, o.to AS until,
       (o.from <= $at AND (o.to IS NULL OR $at < o.to)) AS covers_at,
       o.to IS NULL AS current
ORDER BY since, team
LIMIT 20

Q-RANK-1.purpose: algorithmic cause ranking: algo.pageRank over DEPENDS_ON in the incident's scratch projection (mass flows to upstream nodes many symptoms depend on)
Q-RANK-1.cypher:
CALL algo.pageRank('Node', 'DEPENDS_ON') YIELD node, score
RETURN node.id AS id, score
ORDER BY score DESC, id
LIMIT 50

Q-REM-1.purpose: learned remediation ordering: past incidents that share a Symptom with $inc (or are listed in $incidents), and how each fix kind fared on them: successes (RESOLVED_BY an APPLIED action), failures (a NOT_APPLIED action), Beta(1,1)-smoothed success rate (s+1)/(s+f+2). Per kind (target '*') and per flag for flip_flag; UNKNOWN verdicts count as neither
Q-REM-1.cypher:
MATCH (p:Incident)
WHERE p.id <> $inc AND (p.id IN $incidents OR size([(p)-[:HAS_SYMPTOM]->(y:Symptom) WHERE y.id IN $symptoms | y.id]) > 0)
MATCH (p)-[r:RESOLVED_BY|ATTEMPTED]->(a:Action)
WHERE (type(r) = 'RESOLVED_BY' AND a.verdict = 'APPLIED') OR a.verdict = 'NOT_APPLIED'
WITH p, a, CASE WHEN type(r) = 'RESOLVED_BY' AND a.verdict = 'APPLIED' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS ok
UNWIND (CASE WHEN a.kind = 'flip_flag' THEN ['*', a.target_id] ELSE ['*'] END) AS target
WITH a.kind AS kind, target, toInteger(sum(ok)) AS successes, toInteger(sum(1 - ok)) AS failures, collect(DISTINCT p.id) AS incidents
RETURN kind, target, successes, failures, successes + failures AS n,
       (toFloat(successes) + 1.0) / (toFloat(successes + failures) + 2.0) AS rate,
       size(incidents) AS incident_count, incidents[0..20] AS incidents
ORDER BY rate DESC, n DESC, kind, target
LIMIT 50

Q-REPAIR-TARGETS.purpose: where a measured data repair can be applied: the row-share measurements this run recorded anomalous (Evidence.anomalous, decided in code when recorded), each ABOUT exactly one table and one column, joined to the Transform whose SQL WRITES that table (a source table nobody builds is left out), ordered nearest the confirmed cause first along the proof path ($chain, the gate's G2 chain)
Q-REPAIR-TARGETS.cypher:
MATCH (run:Run {id: $run})-[:HAS_TOOL_CALL]->(:ToolCall)-[:PRODUCED_EVIDENCE]->(e:Evidence {kind: 'row_share'})-[:ABOUT]->(n:Node)
WHERE e.anomalous = true
WITH e, [x IN collect(DISTINCT n.id) WHERE size(split(x, '.')) = 2] AS tables,
     [x IN collect(DISTINCT n.id) WHERE size(split(x, '.')) = 3] AS columns
WHERE size(tables) = 1 AND size(columns) = 1
WITH e, head(tables) AS table, head(columns) AS column
MATCH (t:Transform)-[:WRITES]->(x:Table {id: table})
WITH e, table, column, t, [i IN range(0, size($chain) - 1) WHERE $chain[i] = table | i] AS at
RETURN e.id AS evidence, table, column, e.params AS params, e.value AS share, t.id AS transform,
       [(t)-[:READS]->(r:Table) | r.id] AS reads, CASE WHEN size(at) = 0 THEN size($chain) ELSE at[0] END AS chain_index
ORDER BY chain_index, share DESC, evidence
LIMIT 20

Q-RESIDUE-1.purpose: residue check (advisory, never gating): every component this incident's runs MEASURED anomalous (the same Evidence.anomalous the gate reads), and whether it is downstream of the confirmed cause over the G2 relation set (CHANGED|GATES|PROPAGATES_TO, ≤ 8 hops). Unexplained ones mean another fault may be active
Q-RESIDUE-1.cypher:
MATCH (c:Node {id:$cause})
MATCH (i:Incident {id:$inc})-[:HAS_RUN]->(:Run)-[:HAS_TOOL_CALL]->(:ToolCall)-[:PRODUCED_EVIDENCE]->(e:Evidence)-[:ABOUT]->(n:Node)
WHERE e.anomalous = true AND e.kind IN ['metric', 'profile', 'baseline_comparison', 'row_share', 'error_rate'] AND NOT n:Column
WITH c, n, collect(DISTINCT e.id) AS evidence, collect(DISTINCT e.kind) AS kinds
RETURN n.id AS id, [x IN labels(n) WHERE x <> 'Node'][0] AS label, evidence, kinds,
       size([(c)-[:CHANGED|GATES|PROPAGATES_TO*1..8]->(n) | 1]) > 0 AS explained
ORDER BY explained DESC, id
LIMIT 100

Q-SUS-1.purpose: changes in the window on the symptom or anything upstream of it, with hop distance
Q-SUS-1.cypher:
MATCH (sym:Node {id:$symptom})
CALL { WITH sym CALL algo.SSpaths({sourceNode: sym, relTypes: ['DEPENDS_ON'], weightProp: 'w', relDirection: 'outgoing', maxLen: 8, pathCount: 1000}) YIELD path
       RETURN collect({id: last(nodes(path)).id, hops: length(path)}) AS found }
WITH sym, found + [{id: sym.id, hops: 0}] AS ups
MATCH (d:Deploy) WHERE d.at >= $onset - $window_ms AND d.at <= $onset
WITH ups, d
MATCH (d)-[:CHANGED]->(x)
WITH d, x, [u IN ups WHERE u.id = x.id | u.hops] AS hs
WHERE size(hs) > 0
UNWIND hs AS h
WITH d, x, min(h) AS hops
RETURN d.id AS deploy, d.kind AS kind, x.id AS target, d.at AS at, hops
ORDER BY hops, at DESC, deploy
LIMIT 20

Q-SUS-2.purpose: every change in the window anywhere (this is where look-alike distractors enter)
Q-SUS-2.cypher:
MATCH (d:Deploy)-[:CHANGED]->(x)
WHERE d.at >= $onset - $window_ms AND d.at <= $onset
RETURN d.id AS deploy, d.kind AS kind, x.id AS target, d.at AS at
ORDER BY at DESC, deploy
LIMIT 50

Q-WHATIF-1.purpose: what-if (on a GRAPH.COPY branch with cut edges removed): what can the failing component still reach? (algo.BFS over PROPAGATES_TO)
Q-WHATIF-1.cypher:
MATCH (f:Node {id:$failing})
CALL algo.BFS(f, 8, 'PROPAGATES_TO') YIELD nodes
RETURN [n IN nodes | n.id] AS reached
ORDER BY size(reached)
LIMIT 1

Q-WHATIF-2.purpose: what-if: WCC component ids of the protected entry and the given services on the branch (same id = still connected)
Q-WHATIF-2.cypher:
CALL algo.WCC({nodeLabels: ['Service', 'Datastore', 'Table', 'KPI', 'Dashboard'], relationshipTypes: ['PROPAGATES_TO']}) YIELD node, componentId
WITH node, componentId WHERE node.id IN $ids
RETURN node.id AS id, componentId
ORDER BY id
LIMIT 100
